patch_description:
The previous implementation was fundamentally broken for the actual objective: it returned an empty `column_orderings` list (invalid per-row orderings), fabricated/reconstructed rows via `result_df.loc[i]` with mismatched indices and a `pd.DataFrame(columns=...)` skeleton, inserted a fake `original_index` column, mutated `group.iloc[:, ...]` slices without effect, and its shape/merge assertions could fail (as seen in the stdout, the recursion ran but produced invalid output). It also optimized squared field lengths and value-count heuristics rather than actual character-Trie prefix reuse.

Fix: complete rewrite. Cells are serialized exactly as the evaluator does (missing -> "", else str). Two bounded candidate constructions are built and scored with the true serial-Trie objective (sorted-string adjacent LCP sum, binary-search LCP in C-speed slices):
1. A global frequency-ranked column order scoring sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)).
2. A conditional partition tree using precomputed factorized integer codes: inside each group pick the field with max (count-1)*len savings, partition, recurse with bounded depth, using the global order as deterministic tail.
The candidate with the higher measured LCP reuse wins; per-row column orderings are returned consistent with the permuted cell data. col_merge is honored via the parent's merging_columns with a safe fallback; all values, rows and columns are preserved (object dtype output).
